claims.claim: Any neural network with any activation function can be represented exactly as a decision tree, keeping the network's accuracy exactly as is.
claims.quote: any neural network with any activation function can be represented as a decision tree. The representation is equivalence and not an approximation, thus keeping the accuracy of the neural network exactly as is

claims.claim: An algorithm extracts rules from neural networks by drawing parallels with decision trees, and the extracted rules preserve high predictive accuracy of the original networks.
claims.quote: rules extracted from neural networks are comparable with those of decision trees in terms of predictive accuracy, number of rules and average number of conditions for a rule; they preserve high predictive accuracy of original networks

claims.claim: A trained neural network can be used to create a soft decision tree that generalizes better than one learned directly from the training data.
claims.quote: We describe a way of using a trained neural net to create a type of soft decision tree that generalizes better than one learned directly from the training data

claims.claim: Knowledge distillation of deep neural networks into vanilla decision trees achieves 1% to 5% better accuracy than vanilla decision trees at the same tree depth on multi-class datasets.
claims.quote: the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1% to 5%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth

claims.claim: MIPS uses an integer autoencoder to convert an RNN into a finite state machine, then applies Boolean or integer symbolic regression to capture the learned algorithm as Python code, solving 32 of 62 algorithmic tasks including 13 unsolved by GPT-4.
claims.quote: MIPS uses an integer autoencoder to convert the RNN into a finite state machine, then applies Boolean or integer symbolic regression to capture the learned algorithm. As opposed to large language models, this program synthesis technique makes no use of (and is therefore not limited by) human training data

claims.claim: MIPS solves 32 of 62 algorithmic tasks, including 13 that are not solved by GPT-4.
claims.quote: We test MIPS on a benchmark of 62 algorithmic tasks that can be learned by an RNN and find it highly complementary to GPT-4: MIPS solves 32 of them, including 13 that are not solved by GPT-4 (which also solves 30)

claims.claim: Fuzzy rules can be derived from a fuzzy ARTMAP neural network through pruning and quantization of continuous learned weights, producing compact comprehensible rules with accuracy and complexity comparing favorably to alternative algorithms.
claims.quote: Rule extraction proceeds in two stages: pruning, which simplifies the network structure by removing excessive recognition categories and weights; and quantization of continuous learned weights, which allows the final system state to be translated into a usable set of descriptive rules

claims.claim: ARTMAP rule extraction produces compact sets of comprehensible rules for which accuracy and complexity compare favorably to rules extracted by alternative algorithms.
claims.quote: Simulation results consistently indicate that ARTMAP rule extraction produces compact sets of comprehensible rules for which accuracy and complexity compare favorably to rules extracted by alternative algorithms

claims.claim: Feature maps from the final CNN layer are transformed into a one-dimensional feature vector using a fully connected layer, then used to train a decision tree that achieves performance as good as the CNN with minimum complexity.
claims.quote: The feature maps in the final layer of a CNN are transformed into a one-dimensional feature vector using a fully connected layer. Subsequently, the extracted features are used to train a decision tree to achieve the best accuracy under constraints of depth and nodes

claims.claim: The decision tree performance is observed to be as good as the CNN with minimum complexity on medical image datasets.
claims.quote: We observed that performance of the decision tree is as good as a CNN with minimum complexity

claims.claim: The dsmtree distillation method transfers hierarchical decision logic into neural networks, matching teacher performance within 2% on many benchmarks.
claims.quote: dsmtree, a novel distillation method that transfers hierarchical decision logic into neural networks, matching teacher performance within 2% on many benchmarks

open_questions: What are the computational costs and scalability limits of exact equivalence methods (S1) for large networks?
How much accuracy is lost when distilling to hard decision trees versus soft decision trees (S3)?
What are the fidelity metrics for program synthesis methods like MIPS (S5) beyond task solve rates?
How do distillation methods compare on standard benchmarks with reported accuracy retention percentages?
What are the failure modes when distilling networks with skip connections or normalization layers (mentioned in S1 but not evaluated)?
